img-gyn-cervix.intro: Pelvic MRI is the best test for the cervix: tumor size, parametrial invasion, and vaginal, bladder, or rectal spread. Cervical cancer is intermediate (gray) on T2 against the dark cervical stroma.

plates.title: Cervix MRI: Sagittal T2
plates.caption: Sagittal T2, anterior on the left: a bulky cervical cancer invading the posterior bladder wall (FIGO IVA), with a catheter in the bladder. Source: Otero-García et al., Insights Imaging 2019 (PMC6375059), fig. 17a, CC BY 4.0; arrows removed.

hotspots.label: Cervical Tumor (Intermediate T2)
hotspots.blurb: Brighter than the dark cervical stroma. Measure the largest dimension: ≤2 cm IB1, 2–4 cm IB2, >4 cm IB3.

hotspots.label: Uterine Body
hotspots.blurb: Tumor can extend up into the lower uterine segment (doesn't change FIGO stage, but changes the target).

hotspots.label: Vaginal Fornix / Upper Vagina
hotspots.blurb: Tumor in the upper two-thirds of the vagina = IIA; lower third = IIIA. Vaginal gel helps see it.

hotspots.label: Bladder Wall
hotspots.blurb: Loss of the fat plane or mucosal involvement suggests IVA (confirm with cystoscopy and biopsy).

hotspots.label: Rectum
hotspots.blurb: Rectal mucosal invasion = IVA (confirm with proctoscopy).

plates.title: Cervix MRI: Axial T2 (Parametria)
plates.caption: Placeholder MRI-style slice (axial oblique T2 perpendicular to the cervical canal). Swap in a real de-identified MRI image here.

hotspots.label: Intact Dark Stromal Ring
hotspots.blurb: A preserved low-T2 ring on one side essentially excludes parametrial invasion there.

hotspots.label: Disrupted Ring / Parametrial Invasion
hotspots.blurb: Tumor breaking through the ring with spiculation into the fat = IIB.

hotspots.label: Dilated Ureter
hotspots.blurb: Tumor encasing the ureter causes hydroureter/hydronephrosis = IIIB.

hotspots.label: Pelvic Side Wall
hotspots.blurb: Tumor reaching the side wall muscles/vessels = IIIB.

hotspots.label: Enlarged Obturator Node
hotspots.blurb: Short axis >1 cm or round/necrotic: suspicious (IIIC1 if confirmed by imaging/pathology).

img-gyn-endo.intro: For endometrial cancer, MRI answers two questions before or after surgery: how deep into the myometrium (IA vs IB) and is the cervical stroma involved (stage II).

plates.title: Endometrial MRI: Sagittal T2 + DWI
plates.caption: Placeholder MRI-style slice (sagittal T2 of the uterus with an endometrial tumor). Swap in a real de-identified MRI image here.

hotspots.label: Endometrial Tumor
hotspots.blurb: Intermediate on T2, restricts on DWI, enhances less than the myometrium.

hotspots.label: Junctional Zone
hotspots.blurb: Inner dark band of the myometrium. An intact junctional zone suggests no deep invasion.

hotspots.label: Deep Myometrial Invasion (≥50%)
hotspots.blurb: Tumor reaching the outer half of the myometrium = IB.

hotspots.label: Serosa
hotspots.blurb: Breach = IIIA.

hotspots.label: Cervical Stroma
hotspots.blurb: Invasion of the cervical stroma (not just the glands) = stage II.

hotspots.label: Adnexa
hotspots.blurb: Adnexal involvement = IIIA.

img-gyn-nodes.intro: On CT, nodes are found by following the vessels: every pelvic node group is named for the vessel it hugs. Step down from the para-aortic region to the pelvis, then see what involved nodes look like on PET/CT and in the groin.

plates.title: Axial CT: Para-aortic & Common Iliac (L3–L5)
plates.caption: Contrast CT at L4, near the aortic bifurcation, patient's right on your left (normal study; the patient is male, but the retroperitoneal anatomy is the same). Source: Mikael Häggström, via Wikimedia Commons, CC0.

hotspots.label: Aorta / Left Para-aortic Nodes
hotspots.blurb: Left para-aortic nodes sit beside the aorta.

hotspots.label: IVC / Paracaval Nodes
hotspots.blurb: Right-sided (paracaval and interaortocaval) nodes.

hotspots.label: Kidney
hotspots.blurb: Key OAR for an extended field. The top of the field is usually the renal vessels (T12–L1).

hotspots.label: Small Bowel
hotspots.blurb: Dose-limiting for extended-field RT.

plates.title: Axial CT: Pelvic Nodes (Acetabulum)
plates.caption: Planning CT at the acetabular roof, patient's right on your left. Red = nodal CTV along the pelvic side walls; blue = cervix CTV. Source: Cancers (Basel) 2026 (PMC13465101), fig. 2B, CC BY 4.0.

hotspots.label: External Iliac Nodes
hotspots.blurb: Anterolateral along the vessels.

hotspots.label: Internal Iliac Nodes
hotspots.blurb: Posterior toward the sacrum.

hotspots.label: Obturator Nodes
hotspots.blurb: Medial to the obturator internus.

hotspots.label: Cervix / Parametria
hotspots.blurb: Central target.

hotspots.label: Pelvic Bone Marrow
hotspots.blurb: Marrow-sparing IMRT lowers blood count drops during chemoRT.

gallery.title: PET/CT: para-aortic node
gallery.caption: FDG-avid para-aortic node on fused PET/CT: IIIC2 disease extends the field. Source: J Imaging 2025 (PMC11856187), CC BY 4.0.

gallery.title: Groin CT
gallery.caption: Enlarged inguinal nodes (arrows) around the femoral vessels. Source: Cancers (Basel) 2024 (PMC10813817), CC BY 4.0.

img-gyn-pet.intro: FDG PET/CT is standard for locally advanced cervical cancer (and advanced/high-grade uterine cancer). It maps the nodes, which decide the RT field and the boosts.

plates.title: PET/CT: Nodal and Distant Staging
plates.caption: FDG PET/CT staging of stage IVB cervical cancer. Left: MIP. Middle and right columns: fused PET/CT and CT at the pelvis, the para-aortic region, and the supraclavicular fossa. Source: J Imaging 2025 (PMC11856187), fig. 4, CC BY 4.0; letters and arrows removed.

hotspots.label: Cervical Primary
hotspots.blurb: Intensely avid. PET response at 3 months after chemoRT predicts outcome.

hotspots.label: Pelvic Node (IIIC1)
hotspots.blurb: Avid external iliac or obturator node: boost it (e.g., to 55–60 Gy total).

hotspots.label: Para-aortic Node (IIIC2)
hotspots.blurb: Extended field up to the renal vessels.

hotspots.label: Supraclavicular Node (IVB)
hotspots.blurb: Distant disease; changes intent toward systemic therapy.

hotspots.label: Bladder (Physiologic)
hotspots.blurb: Excreted FDG. Look carefully around it.

hotspots.label: Kidneys (Physiologic)
hotspots.blurb: Normal excretion; also check for hydronephrosis.

img-gyn-ct.intro: CT is used for body staging (lungs, liver, nodes, hydronephrosis) and is the planning scan. The vulva is planned on CT too, with attention to the groins.

plates.title: CT Abdomen/Pelvis: Staging Findings
plates.caption: Staging CT findings, patient's right on your left. Top: right hydronephrosis and a pelvic mass obstructing the ureter (Cureus 2025, PMC12329160, CC BY 4.0). Bottom: omental caking and large-volume ascites (Cureus 2026, PMC13105303, CC BY 4.0).

hotspots.label: Hydronephrosis
hotspots.blurb: In cervical cancer = IIIB unless another cause.

hotspots.label: Ascites
hotspots.blurb: Suggests peritoneal disease (ovarian, serous endometrial).

hotspots.label: Omental Caking
hotspots.blurb: Classic for ovarian / serous cancers.

hotspots.label: Pelvic Mass
hotspots.blurb: Primary tumor.

plates.title: CT Simulation: Pelvic IMRT
plates.caption: Axial planning CT for cervical cancer IMRT, patient's right on your left. Yellow = uterine/primary CTV, red = nodal CTV, pink = involved node. Source: Cancers (Basel) 2026 (PMC13465101), fig. 2A, CC BY 4.0.

hotspots.label: Primary CTV (Cervix, Uterus, Parametria, Upper Vagina)
hotspots.blurb: The whole uterus and cervix, parametria, and upper vagina (more if the vagina is involved).

hotspots.label: Nodal CTV
hotspots.blurb: Obturator, internal/external iliac, presacral, common iliac (± para-aortic) around the vessels.

hotspots.label: Rectum
hotspots.blurb: OAR.

hotspots.label: Pelvic Bone Marrow
hotspots.blurb: Sparing lowers hematologic toxicity with cisplatin.

plates.title: CT Simulation: Vulva & Groins
plates.caption: Axial CT at the femoral heads with inguinal node CTVs (purple). From an anal cancer atlas, but the groin volume is the same one used for vulvar cancer. Source: Cancers (Basel) 2023 (PMC10741760), fig. 2, CC BY 4.0.

hotspots.label: Right Inguinofemoral Nodes
hotspots.blurb: Contour around the femoral vessels; depth varies a lot with body habitus (why CT planning matters).

hotspots.label: Left Inguinofemoral Nodes
hotspots.blurb: Treat bilaterally for midline tumors.

hotspots.label: Femoral Head / Neck
hotspots.blurb: Keep dose down (fracture risk).

hotspots.label: Anus / Rectum
hotspots.blurb: OAR; may be target if involved.

img-gyn-brachy.intro: Image-guided brachytherapy: the applicator is placed in the OR, then an MRI (or CT) is taken with it in place to contour the HR-CTV and organs at risk before each fraction.

plates.title: Brachytherapy: Tandem & Ring on MRI (Sagittal)
plates.caption: Placeholder MRI-style slice (sagittal T2 with a tandem and ring applicator in place). Swap in a real de-identified MRI image here.

hotspots.label: Tandem
hotspots.blurb: Goes through the cervical os into the uterus. Dose falls off steeply around it.

hotspots.label: Ring (or Ovoids)
hotspots.blurb: Sits in the vaginal fornices against the cervix.

hotspots.label: HR-CTV
hotspots.blurb: Whole cervix plus residual tumor at brachy. Goal D90 ≥85 Gy EQD2 (EBRT + brachy).

hotspots.label: Point A
hotspots.blurb: 2 cm above the os along the tandem, 2 cm lateral. The historical prescription point.

hotspots.label: Bladder
hotspots.blurb: D2cc <80–90 Gy EQD2.

hotspots.label: Rectum
hotspots.blurb: D2cc <65–75 Gy EQD2. Vaginal packing or a rectal retractor pushes it away.

hotspots.label: Sigmoid
hotspots.blurb: D2cc <70–75 Gy EQD2. Can drape over the tandem tip.

hotspots.label: Interstitial Needles
hotspots.blurb: Added for bulky or parametrial residual disease that the tandem can't cover.
